name: Ashta Veerattanam — the Eight Shrines of Shiva's Heroic Deeds
theme: Eight Shiva temples, each commemorating one of Shiva's heroic victories over forces of pride and destruction
region: Tamil Nadu (Cuddalore, Kallakurichi, Thanjavur, Mayiladuthurai and Tiruvarur)
description: The Ashta Veerattanam are eight temples of the Tamil country where Shiva is worshipped as Veerattaneswarar, the lord of heroic deeds, each shrine remembering one of his victories. A traditional Tamil verse names them in order: the severing of Brahma's fifth head at Thirukandiyur, the slaying of Andhakasura at Thirukkovilur, the burning of the three flying cities at Thiruvathigai, the destruction of Daksha's sacrifice at Thirupariyalur, the vanquishing of Jalandhara at Thiruvirkudi, the subduing of the elephant demon at Vazhuvur, the burning of Kama at Korukkai and the defeat of Yama to save the boy Markandeya at Thirukkadaiyur. Most of them are Paadal Petra Sthalams praised in the Tevaram. Thiruvathigai holds a special place as the scene of Appar's return to the Shaiva faith, and Thirukkadaiyur, where Markandeya was saved, is where devotees mark sixtieth and eightieth birthdays.
